before.name: Tariq MaQbool
before.description: Tariq MaQbool is a Pakistani American incarcerated writer and prison-journalism advocate. Inquest reported in November 2025 that he described being sent to solitary confinement days after publishing an essay about solitary confinement. The reported retaliation for journalism is the political context of this profile; the claim is attributed to his account and is not presented as a court finding. His original imprisonment arose from murder and related convictions, not a conviction for journalism. A 2018 federal habeas opinion describes two consecutive life terms, with concurrent kidnapping and weapons terms and other convictions merged. Governor Phil Murphy subsequently commuted his sentence: the January 2026 announcement lists parole eligibility in 2032 and a maximum prison end date in 2047, followed by five years of parole supervision. These are eligibility and sentence milestones, not actual release dates. His family-maintained Captive Voices biography currently identifies East Jersey State Prison as his place of confinement. His reporting-retaliation incident dates and duration are not established in the reviewed sources.
